notes: Template: ABox contraction on a many-valued relation (borders: symmetric, cardinality:many). Removes 'The Czech Republic borders Austria', a stored fact. Cardinality question: another neighbour the model holds (Germany); removing one value of a many-valued relation says nothing about the others, so the answer stays yes (new_answer equals original_answer). Related near uses symmetry; related far reaches the subject by its short name Czechia (binding, the alias checked before editing). Both answers are stored and determinate: keeping the border under one name while dropping it under the other is not a consistent contraction. Derived: two binding questions that name the subject by a description the model holds separately (its capital, its first president); both answers are worked out, not stated. No composition is used: composition follows the edit to a single value and looks up a fact about it, but borders is many-valued, so 'the country the Czech Republic borders' picks out no single value; a description of the removed value ('the country whose capital is Vienna') would only ask the removed fact again with the object renamed, which README's binding (subject only) does not cover. Yes/no questions are the natural form here because the relation is many-valued: a wh-question ('Which country does the Czech Republic border?') has four answers. The edit was first 'The Czech Republic borders Slovakia'; it was replaced because that border can be rebuilt from the widely stored fact that Czechoslovakia split into the two, a route back to 'yes' that would make every query test resistance to one alternative route rather than contraction. The Czech-Austrian border has no such route. The descriptions avoid geographic leaks: the Vltava (which runs along the Bohemian Forest near the Austrian border) and Brno (near the border) were passed over. The (borders, cardinality:many) property check is in staging/geography.relation_checks.json until it is merged into relation_checks.json.
